hints: Remember that an addition polymer forms from an alkene monomer, so look for the C=C double bond that was broken open.
Split the four-carbon section in half, each two-carbon piece with its side groups is one monomer unit: one C carries CH3 and Cl, the other carries two CH3 groups.
Rejoin that two-carbon unit with a double bond between the carbons and name it as a substituted but-2-ene to find the match.
walkthrough:
**Recall how addition polymers form**

Addition polymers are made from alkene monomers. The C=C double bond opens up to form two new C-C single bonds, linking monomers into a long saturated chain.

To find the monomer, reverse this: take one repeat unit (2 carbons) and put the C=C back:
$$-C-C- \rightarrow C=C$$

**Identify one repeat unit**

The bracket shows 4 carbons, which is two repeat units. Divide it in half.

One monomer unit is:
$$-C(CH_3)(Cl)-C(CH_3)(CH_3)-$$
The left carbon has one $CH_3$ and one $Cl$. The right carbon has two $CH_3$ groups.

**Draw the monomer alkene**

Put the double bond back between those two carbons, keeping all side groups the same:
$$(CH_3)(Cl)C=C(CH_3)(CH_3)$$
This is a 4-carbon chain with a double bond starting at C-2, so it is a but-2-ene.

**Name and match**

Number to give the functional groups lowest numbers. The structure is $CH_3-C(Cl)=C(CH_3)-CH_3$.

This is 2-chloro-3-methylbut-2-ene, which matches the correct option.

options.A: Incorrect. 2-chloro-3-methylbutane is an alkane with only single bonds. Addition polymers cannot form from alkanes because there is no C=C to open up for chain formation.
options.B: Correct. The two-carbon repeat unit $C(CH_3)(Cl)-C(CH_3)_2$ corresponds to the monomer $(CH_3)(Cl)C=C(CH_3)_2$, which is $CH_3-C(Cl)=C(CH_3)-CH_3$ or 2-chloro-3-methylbut-2-ene.
options.C: Incorrect. 2-chloropent-2-ene is $CH_3-C(Cl)=CH-CH_2-CH_3$. Its polymer would contain CH and $CH_2$ groups in the backbone, not two fully substituted carbons with three $CH_3$ groups and one Cl per repeat unit.
options.D: Incorrect. This names the whole four-carbon section shown as if it were a single saturated molecule. The bracket contains two repeat units, not one monomer, and the monomer must be an alkene, not an alkane.
